claim: The non-bounding expressions in [9iii] “consist of those that function as bounding frequency adjuncts (other than never) together with a postmodifier that cancels the bounding effect”.
evidence_summary: The same page lists never in [9i] under “The form of non-bounding frequency adjuncts”, and its inventory of bounding forms leaves it out: “The class of bounding frequency expressions contains the adverbs once and twice (and archaic thrice), NPs with times as head, PPs consisting of on + NP with occasion as head”. It glosses frequency never as universal, “always doesn’t”.
finding: Medium confidence: the parenthesis puts never among the bounding adjuncts, against [9i] and the inventory on the same page. Page 714’s “except in the special case of one or zero quantity” may explain the motive (never as zero times), but doesn’t remove the conflict.

evidence.example: Page 715 [9i], and the inventory of bounding forms before [8].
evidence.establishes: The parenthesis classes never against the page’s own lists.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
